chapter: Billy Berg's, Granz and Nat Cole
title: The Nat Cole, Lester Young, Callender trio sides
summary: Made for fun at Ben Wallach's studio after Oscar Moore failed to show; Callender praises Granz's fairness and recalls Phineas Newborn at Normandie Hall.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Oh yeah, it's all recorded. It's on record somewhere. And it was soon after this that Nat and Lester and I did the 12-inch...the big record on "Tea For Two," "Indiana," "Body and Soul" and "I Can't Get Started." This was done in Ben Wallach's recording studio, which at the

time was on the corner of Sunset and Vine. Oscar Moore was supposed to have shown up, and he didn't show up so we decided we'd do it, we'd just do it -- because we liked to play together. So this has since become a part of jazz history. Every now and then a new release turns up somewhere. We didn't really make any money for doing the date, because it wasn't a date; it was just for pleasure. I think Norman has forgotten that it was for pleasure, because I've seen different reports about it. But from the horse's mouth, that was done just for fun. However, we did get paid later for it, and we still receive royalties whenever it shows up, so...
That beats some of the other...

Well, Norman has always been fair to musicians, I have to say. Because without us, he never would have gotten started. We used to do those things at Normandie Hall that you were talking... We used to do those for ten dollars or whatever he could afford at the time. If he didn't make any money, we didn't make any. But it was okay. We just liked to play. That's the first place I heard Phineas Newborn, when he was 17, at Normandie Hall.
He came in and astounded everybody -- except Art Tatum, that is.
